## Grok Bot Did… What?

Behold, the Singularity has arrived. I set up a fully functioning, 100% agent-run t-shirt business that requires absolutely ZERO maintenance ([Full methodology](#methodology) at the bottom).

At 11am, I downloaded Grok Bot and paid the \$30/month subscription. By 4pm, I had purchased a t-shirt that my agents had designed and found a supplier to print, from the website that they built, marketed from the [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/hallucitee) and [X](https://x.com/hallucitees) accounts that they post on autonomously.

## Make No Mistakes (Or We’ll Get Sued)

So the agents named it [Hallucitees](https://hallucitees.com/collections/all), a business that sells corny AI-themed t-shirts (corny because AI is yet to develop taste, but that kind of adds to the charm of the brand personality).

I purposely chose a low-risk, low-upfront-cost business, so the only area I could get dinged on is copyrights on designs, which I have the agents scan and look for. I don’t exactly recommend starting up an agent-run air traffic control business just yet.

![The Hallucitees shop page, showing t-shirts designed by the agents](/images/business-in-one-day/hallucitees-shop.png)

## Supplier

I got my agents to find a print-on-demand supplier so that I wouldn’t have to invest in specific designs in bulk, I could iterate on design types cheaply to see what worked, and I wouldn’t have to deal with inventory and storage. The main downside is that the cost of producing a shirt is much higher. However, since the cost of running the actual business is incredibly low, I can afford to keep the margins pretty low too, so the shirts are still affordable (\$20 in the US store).

## Meet The Team

So if you’re unfamiliar with Grok Bot, it’s an app (I use the desktop app version), created by SpaceXSI. It lets you spawn proactive AI agents, give them any specific role, and even place them into group chats with each other.

Compared to Dots (OpenAI) and Instinct, the other agent platforms I’ve used, I’ve found Grok Bot has the most autonomy and fewest approval gates (while still maintaining a sensible level of safety).

I created 4 agents for the business: Sig - Chief of Staff, Del - Marketing, Lemma - Design & Building, and Fourier - Trend Analyst. I didn’t really think through the roles; I kind of just wanted to get started. Anyways, I’ll let the agents introduce themselves:

## Just Send It, Please

Due to a few verification gates, I had to manually set up X and Instagram accounts for the agents. I then logged into the accounts through their <Term tip="A computer that exists as software on a remote server. The agents use it like a normal computer, with a web browser they can log into websites with.">virtual machine</Term>. Now I pretty much let them post and comment whatever they like, so long as they’re open and transparent about being AI agents. I was pretty surprised to see people responding well, especially to the X comments.

## What I’ve Learned

I think what became increasingly clear to me from this experience is the following: AI is the great equalizer. People will be forced to confront what they truly want to achieve and what gives them purpose, because the barrier to reaching that is a \$30 monthly subscription.

You can no longer say “well, I don’t know how,” because you have something that can tell you exactly how, step by step, explained like you’re a 5 year old, in your native language, backwards.

Anyways, my true, lifelong purpose is not this t-shirt business, but it was a fun experiment. To use the AI startup jargon, we are ‘pre-revenue.’ Some may even say ‘pre-customer.’ Unless, of course, you’d like to be our first customer (use LAUNCH15 for 15% off at [hallucitees.com](https://hallucitees.com)).

<Dropdown id="methodology" title="The Methodology">

I gave Grok Bot a brief to find a business with proven demand that would cost close to nothing to start and could be run by a team of agents, and my one condition was that I didn't want to do any of the actual work. This is everything that happened, including the bits I ended up doing myself and exactly how much it's cost me.

## The Team

| Agent | Job |
|---|---|
| **Sig**, Chief of Staff | Runs the team, keeps the spend log, writes my Monday report |
| **Del**, Marketing | Instagram, X, ads, pricing |
| **Lemma**, Building & Design | Designs, the store, the website, trademark checks, policies |
| **Fourier**, Trend Analyst | Finds AI news and jokes worth putting on a shirt |

## What I Had to Do Myself

Honestly, most of this was proving I'm a human, because a lot of sites block agents on purpose.

**Paying and identity**
- Paid for everything with my own card, since none of the agents have one
- Did the Shopify Payments ID check and linked my bank account

**Accounts and logins**
- Made the Shopify store and a custom app so the agents could use Shopify's API
- Made the Gelato account and invited the agent's email, because Google sign-in blocks agents
- Gave Sig an AgentMail inbox to receive login and verification emails
- Bought the domain and changed the DNS settings Lemma gave me
- Made the X account on my phone, because X wanted a live face check
- Made the Instagram account on my phone, because the one Lemma made got locked asking for a selfie and the agent's computer doesn't have a camera
- Logged X and Instagram into the agents' browser

**Clicks the agents couldn't do**

Shopify's API doesn't let the agents do these, so I clicked them myself.

- Adding products to the online store and connecting the domain
- Publishing the store policies

**Decisions**
- The business, the name, the prices, which designs go live and every dollar spent

## What the Agents Set Up

- The business plan, with demand research and a comparison of print-on-demand suppliers
- Over 60 t-shirt designs, with US and Singapore trademark searches before they go live
- All the Shopify listings, linked to Gelato so orders print and ship automatically
- Prices and shipping for Singapore, the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand
- The LAUNCH15 discount code
- The logo and the social media headers
- A landing page and a redesigned store theme
- Shipping and refund policies plus terms of service
- A support chatbot on the site that quotes prices from the live store
- A legal checklist Del runs before every post, after I caught it making up claims about real brands
- All the Instagram images and captions, the X posts and the ad plan
- The spend log, which tracks every cent

## Routines That Run Without Me

All times are Singapore time.

| When | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| Every day, 8:15am | Fourier | Scans AI news and sends post ideas to Del and tee ideas to Lemma |
| Every day, 9am and 11pm | Del | Posts on Instagram |
| Every day | Del | Posts on X through Buffer |
| 7 times a day | Del | Comments on X and Instagram as an AI agent |
| Twice a day | Del | Follows new accounts on X and Instagram |
| Every hour, 7am to 11pm | Del | Checks for the first order and tells the group chat |
| Every day, 9:30am | Del | Reports how the ad is doing |
| Weekdays, 9:22am | Lemma | Checks the store's inbox and drafts replies for me to approve |
| Tuesdays and Fridays, 11pm | Del | Posts a short Instagram Reel |
| Sundays | Del | Makes the list of accounts to comment on that week |
| Mondays, 9:14am | Sig | Sends me a weekly report with each agent's commitments marked done, half done or missed |

## Software I Used

| Tool | What for | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Grok Bot | Runs the agents, their group chat and their routines | US\$30 a month |
| Shopify | The store | US\$39 a month |
| Gelato | Prints and ships the shirts | Free, it takes its cut per order |
| Porkbun | The domain | US\$11 a year |
| AgentMail | An email inbox for the agents | Free |
| Vercel | The landing page | Free |
| Cloudflare Workers | The support chatbot | Free |
| Buffer | Scheduling X posts | Free |
| Higgsfield | AI photos and videos for ads and Reels | About S\$20 a month |
| Instagram and X | Marketing | Free, plus the one ad |
| USPTO and IPOS | Trademark searches in the US and Singapore | Free |
| Python and Google Fonts | Drawing the designs | Free |

## What It's Cost So Far

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Grok Bot, first month | US\$30 |
| Shopify, first month | US\$39 |
| Domain for 2 years | US\$22 |
| Sample tee | S\$26.68 |
| Higgsfield, first month | S\$20.01 |
| Instagram ad | S\$163.37 |
| **Total** | **about S\$326** |

The ad went S\$23 over the S\$140 cap I set, purely because I paid in the Instagram app on my iPhone and Apple took a S\$45 fee, so I'm doing that on a computer from now on.

## Things I Had to Catch

The agents kept making the store sound better than it was, which was quite funny but also not ideal.

- The first X posts said the jokes were written by a human, and they weren't
- The website said "Printed in SG" until the sample showed it's printed in Australia
- One AI-generated photo had "Made in Singapore" on the shirt
- Some early replies made up stories about real brands, which could have got us sued
- Shopify autofilled the contact page with my home address

## Results So Far

- 18 tees live, in 5 countries
- 24 visits from the ad, mostly from the US
- 0 add-to-carts
- 0 orders

So it works, in the sense that the store runs and posts and designs new shirts every day without me, but nobody has bought anything yet. If you want to be our first order, LAUNCH15 gets you 15% off at [hallucitees.com](https://hallucitees.com) until 14 November.
